title: Computer Networks
subject: core-cs
description: A layer-by-layer study of how computer networks operate, from physical transmission and link-layer protocols through IP routing to TCP, UDP and the application protocols of the Internet. Emphasis is on quantitative analysis: delay, capacity, subnetting and protocol behaviour.

units.title: Unit 1 · Network Foundations
units.description: Reference models, encapsulation, performance metrics and the physical layer.

topics.title: Layered Models: OSI and TCP/IP
topics.description: The seven OSI layers, the TCP/IP model, PDUs and encapsulation.

documents.title: OSI and TCP/IP Models — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Layer functions, PDU names, OSI-to-TCP/IP mapping and a worked encapsulation-overhead example.

topics.title: Performance and the Physical Layer
topics.description: Bandwidth, throughput, the four delay components, bandwidth-delay product, channel capacity and transmission media.

documents.title: Network Performance and the Physical Layer — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Delay formulas with a worked example, bandwidth-delay product, Nyquist and Shannon capacity, and guided versus unguided media.

units.title: Unit 2 · Data Link and Network Layers
units.description: Framing, error control, medium access, Ethernet switching, IP addressing and routing protocols.

topics.title: Data Link Layer: Framing, Error Control and MAC
topics.description: Framing methods, parity, Hamming codes, CRC, ARQ protocols, CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA, Ethernet and switches.

documents.title: Framing, Error Detection and Reliable Delivery — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Bit and byte stuffing, Hamming distance, a worked CRC division, and Stop-and-Wait, Go-Back-N and Selective Repeat with window limits.

documents.title: Medium Access Control, Ethernet and Switching
documents.description: ALOHA, CSMA variants, CSMA/CD versus CSMA/CA, the Ethernet frame format and the switch self-learning algorithm.

topics.title: IP Addressing, Subnetting and Routing
topics.description: IPv4 header, classful and CIDR addressing, subnetting, NAT, IPv6 and routing algorithms and protocols.

documents.title: IP Addressing, Subnetting and Routing — Lecture Notes
documents.description: IPv4 header fields, a /26 subnetting example, NAT, IPv6, distance-vector versus link-state routing and a RIP/OSPF/BGP comparison.

documents.title: Subnetting Practice Problems — Worked Solutions
documents.description: Seven solved problems covering network and broadcast addresses, fixed-length subnetting, VLSM, summarisation and longest prefix match.

units.title: Unit 3 · Transport and Application Layers
units.description: End-to-end transport with TCP and UDP, and the core Internet application protocols.

topics.title: TCP and UDP
topics.description: Ports, segment formats, connection management, flow control and congestion control.

documents.title: TCP and UDP — Lecture Notes
documents.description: UDP and TCP headers, the three-way handshake and teardown, RTO estimation, flow control and Reno congestion control with a cwnd trace.

topics.title: Application Layer Protocols: DNS, HTTP and Email
topics.description: DNS resolution and records, HTTP methods, status codes and versions, email protocols and the TLS handshake.

documents.title: Application Layer Protocols: DNS, HTTP, Email and TLS — Lecture Notes
documents.description: DNS hierarchy and record types, HTTP semantics and HTTP/1.1 versus HTTP/2 versus HTTP/3, SMTP/POP3/IMAP and TLS 1.3.
